best_for: Firefox users who keep dozens of tabs open across projects and want workspaces and split view without leaving Firefox Sync behind.
description:
Zen is a web browser started by developer Mauro V. and built by a small team of volunteers and designers. Its whole layout is designed around vertical tabs down the side of the window, and the team says it has no plans to add horizontal tabs or a phone version.

You can pop a video out into a floating window that stays on top, resize it from any corner and control it from the keyboard. Zen can also slip a playing video into a mini player when you switch tabs, once you turn that on. A small change in about:config lets you scroll through tabs with the mouse wheel. One thing to know first: on Windows and macOS it cannot play DRM-protected streams yet, so Netflix, Spotify and Disney+ will not work in it.

points.title: Firefox underneath
points.text: Zen's code is derived from Firefox. It works with Firefox Sync, so your bookmarks, passwords, history and add-ons can follow you from an existing Firefox setup.

points.title: Tabs grouped by project
points.text: Workspaces keep separate sets of tabs per project. Split view shows two tabs side by side, compact mode hides the tab bar, and Glance helps you jump back to tabs you use often.

points.title: Themes through mods
points.text: A mods registry offers community themes and tweaks, and you can edit the browser's CSS live if you want to go further.

points.title: Free and open source
points.text: Zen is MPL-2.0 software with no paid tier, built by a core team and outside contributors and supported by donations.

points.title: Releases come often
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 173 versions, which shows how often Zen ships. Windows installers are machine-wide for x64 and Arm64; macOS gets one universal build and only the current release is listed.

points.title: Linux is not listed here
points.text: This page covers Windows and macOS only. On Linux, Zen's own download page offers x86_64 and aarch64 tarballs and a Flathub install.
